channel.title: ConstructionDive – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from ConstructionDive – Bias and Credibility (constructiondive.com)

item.title: 3 ways public–private partnerships are strengthening the construction workforce
item.description: CEOs rethink workforce strategy through nonprofit partnerships to expand and stabilize labor pipelines.

item.title: To make housing more affordable, invest in infrastructure
item.description: Homes need roads, water systems and power to serve them. A good start is renewing the federal surface transportation funding set to expire in September, writes a building materials executive.

item.title: Messer-Sundt JV starts $900M Nashville airport infrastructure work
item.description: The job, which will create a road loop and six-level consolidated rental car facility, is part of a broader $3 billion capital plan for the busiest airport in Tennessee.

item.title: Office-to-housing conversion initiatives proliferate in California
item.description: State policymakers have been pursuing policy changes that remove barriers to converting older commercial buildings into housing, with mixed success.

item.title: New York City’s data center opportunity may lie on the ‘edge’: panel
item.description: Demand for data center construction is colliding with the city’s aging power grid, according to a New York Build 2026 panel session.

item.title: AI doesn’t know what your safety experts know: data application specialist
item.description: Grounded, confined questions and strong data can help make AI a much more useful tool for identifying safety trends, said Adam Logan, executive vice president of application and data at ISN.

item.title: Data center boom failed to lift construction spending to start 2026
item.description: The lackluster spending report is “especially concerning in light of the ongoing conflict in Iran,” said Anirban Basu, ABC chief economist.

item.title: City officials urge federal grant application reform
item.description: The “mind-numbing” grant application process could be improved through preparation, intention and building connections, city leaders said during a National League of Cities panel.

item.title: $4.4B Brent Spence Bridge project targets spring groundbreaking
item.description: The work package, which will be constructed by a JV of Walsh Construction and Kokosing, has seen its price tag rise by approximately $700 million due to increases in highway construction costs.

item.title: Feds flow $889M to Western states for water infrastructure
item.description: California will receive $540 million of the funds allocated via President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
